'''Nicole F. Bell''' (born 1975) is an Australian physicist who is a professor at the [[University of Melbourne]]. She is a theoretical physicist who works on dark matter, [[neutrino]] physics, and other topics in particle and astroparticle theory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nicole Bell |url=http://www.stemwomen.org.au/ |access-date=2022-04-24 |website=STEM Women |language=en}}</ref>  

Bell is president of the [[Australian Institute of Physics]]. She was awarded the 2020 [[Australian Academy of Science]] Nancy Millis Medal for her work on dark matter and particle theory.

== Education and career ==
Bell is from [[Australia]]. She earned her doctorate at the [[University of Melbourne]] with thesis research on neutrino oscillations and the early universe.<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Neutrino oscillations and the early universe |date=2000 |language=English |first=Nicole F |last=Bell|oclc=222921402 }}</ref> After earning her doctorate, Bell moved to the [[United States]] and joined the [[Fermilab Center for Particle Astrophysics]] as a research fellow. After three years at Fermilab, Bell was awarded a Sherman Fairchild Prize Fellowship at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=CV {{!}} Nicole Bell |url=https://blogs.unimelb.edu.au/nicole-bell/home/publications/ |access-date=2022-04-24 |language=en-AU}}</ref>

Bell returned to the [[University of Melbourne]] in 2007.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=New hands at the helm, galactic evolution, Science Meets Parliament, and old computers the size of wardrobes {{!}} Australian Institute of Physics |url=https://physics.org.au/new-hands-at-the-helm-galactic-evolution-science-meets-parliament-and-old-computers-the-size-of-wardrobes/ |access-date=2022-04-24 |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2011, she became a Chief Investigator of the [[Australian Research Council]] Centre of Excellence for [[Particle physics|Particle Physics]] at the Terascale, and in 2020, the Theory Program leader of the ARC Centre of Excellence for Dark Matter Particle Physics.<ref name=":2" />

In 2021 Bell was elected vice president of the [[Australian Institute of Physics]].<ref name=":3"/> Bell became president of the Australian Institute of Physics in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Durrani |first=Matin |date=2023-03-17 |title=Ask me anything: Nicole Bell – 'Collaboration is the norm: we achieve more when we work together' |url=https://physicsworld.com/ask-me-anything-nicole-bell-collaboration-is-the-norm-we-achieve-more-when-we-work-together/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
* 2001 Bragg Gold Medal in Physics<ref>{{Cite web |title= Bragg Gold Medal for Excellence in Physics |url=http://aip.org.au/BRAGG-MEDAL |access-date=2022-04-24}}</ref>
* 2012 [[Australian Research Council]] Future Fellowship<ref>{{Cite web |title=ARC Future Fellows announced {{!}} CoEPP |url=http://www.coepp.org.au/news/arc-future-fellows-announced |access-date=2022-04-24 |website=www.coepp.org.au}}</ref>
* 2016 Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] ''"for fundamental contributions regarding the interface of astrophysics and particle physics, particularly in neutrino astrophysics and cosmology, and dark matter phenomenology."''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2016&unit_id=DAP&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|access-date=24 September 2020}}</ref>
* 2020 Elected Fellow of the [[Australian Institute of Physics]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=AIP Fellows |url=https://www.aip.org.au/PUBLIC-FELLOWS-LIST|language=en-AU}}</ref>
* 2020 Australian Academy of Science [[Nancy Millis Medal for Women in Science]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 Nancy Millis Medal for Women in Science |url=https://www.science.org.au/supporting-science/awards-and-opportunities-2/honorific-awardees/2020-awardees#millis |access-date=2022-04-24 |website=Australian Academy of Science |language=en-AU}}</ref>
* 2026 Elected [[List of fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nicole Bell |url=https://science.org.au/about-us/academy-fellows/discover-our-fellows/nicole-bell |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=Australian Academy of Science}}</ref>
